title: CI prints tracker record content to stdout, so a record quoting a workflow-command line forges a failure annotation on a green job
description:
The Tracker integrity job's "Tracker reads cleanly" step (.github/workflows/ci.yml:342-343) runs `quest task list --json` with stdout unredirected. That stdout is the full task-record JSON — every summary, note and comment — and the runner parses workflow-command lines out of a step's own stdout. So a record whose text contains a line like `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` — a session quoting a CI log into a note — becomes a REAL failure-level annotation on a job that is green.

MEASURED 2026-09-30 (this repository):
- Check-run 110060733763 (Tracker integrity, push run 36766159140 on landing 846233e1) concludes success with every step success, yet carries a failure-level annotation whose 4096-char message is note text from .quest/completed/LCLI-507.json. Re-verified in-repo by reading the records: the literal `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` is present in .quest/completed/LCLI-507.json and .quest/tasks/LCLI-516.json.
- The same failure-level annotation is on check-run 110058245909 and on the previous landing 739f2b48's two Tracker integrity check-runs — it had been firing on green runs for days before it was traced.
- opum-agent located the source (OPAG-953; the same unredirected line exists in 8 other fleet repositories, OPAG-971): the job-log line carrying the annotation falls inside this step, which prints every record to stdout.

IMPACT: record text is arbitrary and session-written. The same mechanism would honour `::add-mask::`, `::stop-commands::`, `::warning::` or `::error::` emitted from a note — log masking, command suppression, or forged annotations, sourced from data. This is the same defect class as LCLI-636 (raw input printed inside workflow-command lines), from the read side: there it was an input echoed by a release script, here it is a tracker record echoed by CI.

FIX DIRECTION (design is this repository's to settle): redirect the read to a file under $RUNNER_TEMP, keep the read's exit code as the gate, and print a record count as the positive control so the step reports how much it read and fails on zero. Then inventory the other CI steps that print tracker or docs content to stdout (`quest agents --check`, `lore check`, `lore agents --check`, and release.yml's lore/quest steps) and apply the same discipline wherever they can echo free text — redirect, or record why they cannot.

REFERENCES: OPAG-953 (orchestrator's own fix branch), OPAG-971 (fleet-wide notice), LCLI-636 (prior art, same class, Done), LCLI-507 and LCLI-516 (the records carrying the literal).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 'Tracker reads cleanly' step runs `quest task list --json` with stdout redirected to a file, so no record JSON reaches the runner's log or workflow-command parser, and the step still fails on the tracker read's own non-zero exit.
The step's log states how many task records it read, and the step fails when that count is zero.

Two measurements ride the PR: the changed step green on a normal tree showing its count line, and the same step red (non-zero exit, the tracker's duplicate-identity error text) against a deliberate duplicate record in a scratch fixture — with the commands recorded.
A test in test/ci-workflow.test.ts pins the redirected form and fails if the unredirected `quest task list --json` run line returns.

Every CI step that prints tracker or docs record content to stdout is inventoried in the PR (at least ci.yml's quest and lore steps and release.yml's), each redirected the same way or recorded with the reason it cannot echo free text.

implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED on branch fix/LCLI-661-redirect-tracker-read (PR to follow).

ci.yml: the "Tracker reads cleanly" step now redirects `quest task list --json` stdout AND stderr to $RUNNER_TEMP, gates on the read's own exit status, replays the tracker's own error text only on failure inside a ::stop-commands:: block, and prints the record count as the positive control (zero fails the step). The sibling quest/lore steps — "Managed instructions are current", "lore check", "lore agents --check (bridge currency)" — run through the new scripts/ci-quiet-gate.sh, which captures both streams to files and replays them between stop-commands markers with the child's exit status unchanged.

MEASURED (step body extracted from ci.yml, not retyped):
- green on the real tree: `read 657 task record(s)`, exit 0 (657 = 466 under .quest/tasks + 191 under .quest/completed).
- red on a scratch fixture with LCLI-507 duplicated into both tasks/ and completed/: exit 5, the tracker's own duplicate-identity envelope replayed inside the stop-commands block, our ::error:: line outside it.
- mutation proofs, each mutant built from the defect's shape, each predicting a subset: un-redirect the read -> 2 red/36 green; guard streams instead of replaying -> 2 red; guard exits 0 regardless of child status -> 1 red; unguard a sibling -> 2 red.
- local gates: typecheck exit 0; lint:shell clean (10 tracked .sh); test/ci-workflow.test.ts 38/38; `bun run lore check` exit 0.

ENVIRONMENT, recorded because it falsifies a live handoff trap: this workstation's global `quest` is now 0.12.0 and `bun run lore check` exits 0 locally. The LCLI-650 pair-lock trap written on LCLI-621 ("this workstation's global quest is 0.11.0; verify local gates via a temporary 0.12.0 prefix") is stale as of this session. Nothing in this branch depends on that either way.
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#455 (squash d4427205 on dev; promoted to main by #456, so origin/main == origin/dev == d4427205 at close). Validated by CI run 36795179650 on head 7a76b170: all six required contexts green, the ubuntu leg a labelled RETRY-GREEN (attempt 1 hung on the known Linux epoll race, attempt 2 passed).

The "Tracker reads cleanly" step now redirects `quest task list --json` stdout and stderr to $RUNNER_TEMP, gates on the read's own exit status, replays the tracker's error text only on failure inside a ::stop-commands:: block (newline-safe), and prints the record count as the positive control (zero fails the step). The sibling quest/lore steps run through the new scripts/ci-quiet-gate.sh (mode 100755), which captures both streams and replays them inside the same markers with the child's exit status unchanged.

Measured on the merged head: the Tracker integrity check-run carries ZERO annotations — the pre-fix control, check-run 110060733763 on 846233e1, carried a failure-level annotation forged from .quest/completed/LCLI-507.json, which is still in the repository unchanged; and the job log contains "read 657 task record(s)" with zero occurrences of the forged literal, which the old green job's log carried once. Six mutation cycles, each mutant built from the defect's shape and each reddening exactly its predicted test subset (table in the PR body).

An adversarial reviewer pass ran before the merge and found the change dead on arrival in CI — the script was committed mode 100644 while every routed step invoked it by path, so three required contexts failed with Permission denied (exit 126) while the local suite was 38/38 green. Fixed with the mode plus a test that reads the GIT INDEX for every script a workflow invokes by path. The same pass found a stop-commands gluing hole (a stream not ending in a newline glues to the resume marker and leaves the block open), five holes in the first sweep, and two unpinned guard properties; all fixed, each with a mutant.

Tracker records filed alongside: LCLI-660 gained the epoll rate data point (this branch's runs hung on all four attempts across its first two runs) and LCLI-645 gained its AC1 measurement (the released quest 0.12.0 fails link-quest-race's workspace-wide-revision positive control exactly as that task records).
